section: Kakatiyas - origins, Beta I, Rudradeva, Ganapatideva; Kakatiya-Yadava-Hoysala relations
subsections: Legacy link to the Vijayanagara founders

accepted.s: Who killed Rudradeva and captured Ganapatideva?
accepted.x: Yadava ruler Jaitugi killed Rudradeva and captured Ganapatideva during the Kakatiya-Yadava conflict.
accepted.tq: Use the ruler–event association and eliminate opponents belonging to other conflicts.

accepted.s: Which development contributed to Yadava Jaitugi releasing Ganapatideva?
o: The invasion of the Krishna-Tungabhadra region by Veera Ballala II
The revolt of the Nellore Chodas
The defeat of the Pandyas at Muttukur
The capture of Kanchi by Rudramadevi
accepted.x: Hoysala Veera Ballala II pushed into the Krishna-Tungabhadra region, compelling Jaitugi to release Ganapatideva.
accepted.tq: Identify the cause-and-effect link rather than merely recalling the names of the rulers.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the later Kakatiya conflicts?
o: Rudramadevi repulsed the Yadava Mahadeva, while Pedarudru defeated Hoysala Ballala III after 1316.
Rudramadevi was defeated by Yadava Mahadeva, while Pedarudru supported Hoysala Ballala III.
Mahadeva defeated Rudramadevi and captured the Kakatiya capital after 1316.
Pedarudru defeated Yadava Jaitugi and installed Rudramadevi on the throne.
accepted.x: Rudramadevi repulsed Yadava Mahadeva, and Prataparudra’s commander Pedarudru defeated Hoysala Ballala III after 1316.
accepted.tq: Split the paired ruler–opponent relationships before selecting the precisely matched statement.

accepted.s:
Consider the following pairs:
1. Recherla Rudra — Kakatiya Rajya Bharadhureya
2. Prasadaditya — Kakatiya Rajya Sthapanacharya
3. Malyala Chauda Senani — Chouda Samudram
4. Kamasani — Gudur inscription
Which of the pairs given above are correctly matched?
accepted.x: All four pairs are correctly matched. Recherla Rudra bore the title Kakatiya Rajya Bharadhureya; Prasadaditya was Sthapanacharya; Chauda Senani built Chouda Samudram; and Kamasani’s role is recorded in the Gudur inscription.
accepted.tq: Verify each family–member–title or achievement pair independently before using the coded options.

accepted.s: Who among the following was associated with the titles ‘Kakatiya Rajya Sthapanacharya’ and ‘Raya Pitamahanka’?
accepted.x: Prasadaditya of the Kayastha family bore the titles Kakatiya Rajya Sthapanacharya and Raya Pitamahanka.
accepted.tq: Distinguish similar feudatory titles by linking the title to the correct family member.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Kamasani — Made Garuda Beta a Chalukya vassal
Malyala Chauda Senani — Built Ramappa temple
accepted.x: Malyala Chauda Senani built Chouda Samudram. The Ramappa temple and tank at Palampet are associated with Recherla Rudra.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped achievement among closely related Kakatiya feudatories.

accepted.s: Which family of Kakatiya feudatories is associated with Kamasani?
accepted.x: Kamasani belonged to the Viriyala family and made Garuda Beta a Chalukya vassal, as recorded in the Gudur inscription.
accepted.tq: Use the family–member association to separate the four feudatory groups.

accepted.s: Recherla Rudra is associated with which combination?
o: Saving the kingdom during Ganapati’s captivity and constructing the Ramappa temple and tank at Palampet
Restoring Manumasiddhi II and serving as an envoy to the Pandyas
Building Chouda Samudram and making Garuda Beta a Chalukya vassal
Defeating Hoysala Ballala III and ruling the Nellore region
accepted.x: Recherla Rudra saved the kingdom during Ganapati’s captivity and is associated with the Ramappa temple and tank at Palampet.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure achievement and reject combinations assembled from different feudatories.

accepted.s: Who was the father of Harihara and Bukka, the founders of the Vijayanagara ruling house?
accepted.x: Sangama, the father of Harihara and Bukka, was a Kakatiya chief. The brothers had served the Kakatiyas before founding Vijayanagara in 1336.
accepted.tq: Use the dynastic legacy link rather than confusing the Kakatiya chief with a later ruler.
accepted.sec: Legacy link to the Vijayanagara founders

accepted.s: The brothers Harihara and Bukka are associated with which sequence?
o: Serving the Kakatiyas, followed by the foundation of Vijayanagara in 1336
Founding Vijayanagara, followed by service under the Kakatiyas in 1336
Serving the Pandyas, followed by the foundation of Warangal in 1263
Serving the Hoysalas, followed by the restoration of Nellore in 1159
accepted.x: Harihara and Bukka served the Kakatiyas before founding Vijayanagara in 1336.
accepted.tq: Arrange the two linked stages by identifying the earlier service and the later foundation.
accepted.sec: Legacy link to the Vijayanagara founders

accepted.s: Who restored Manumasiddhi II of Nellore to his throne?
accepted.x: Ganapatideva intervened in Nellore affairs and restored Manumasiddhi II to the throne. The poet Tikkana went as envoy to seek Ganapatideva’s help.
accepted.tq: Match the political intervention with the ruler who carried it out.

accepted.s: Who went as an envoy to seek Ganapatideva’s help for Manumasiddhi II?
accepted.x: The poet Tikkana went as an envoy to request Ganapatideva’s intervention on behalf of Manumasiddhi II.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the literary figure acting as envoy from military commanders and feudatories.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements is correct about Ganapatideva?
o: After the Muttukur defeat, he nevertheless retained firm control over coastal Andhra.
After the Muttukur defeat, he abandoned all control over coastal Andhra.
He ruled only the Nellore region after restoring Manumasiddhi II.
He transferred coastal Andhra to the Yadavas after his release.
accepted.x: Although Ganapatideva was defeated at Muttukur, he continued to hold coastal Andhra firmly.
accepted.tq: Watch for the extreme reversal in statements claiming complete loss of territory.

accepted.s: Which title was borne by Ganapatideva in recognition of his authority over the Telugu country?
accepted.x: Ganapatideva bore the title Andhra Deshadhiswara and is associated with the unification of Telugudesam.
accepted.tq: Separate a ruler’s sovereign title from the titles of his feudatories.

accepted.s: As a boy, Ganapatideva was held captive by which ruler?
accepted.x: Ganapatideva was held captive as a boy by Yadava ruler Jaitugi. Recherla Rudra later crushed revolts and installed him.
accepted.tq: Differentiate the captor from the later Yadava ruler involved in the revenge war.

accepted.s: Which pair is correctly matched?
o: Velanati Chodas — Defeated Ganapatideva at Muttukur in 1263
Pandyas — Made Vellanki Gangadhara viceroy of Sabbinadu
accepted.x: The Yadavas captured Ganapatideva. The Pandyas defeated him at Muttukur; Velanati Chodas killed Prola II; and Rudradeva appointed Vellanki Gangadhara viceroy of Sabbinadu.
accepted.tq: Identify the correctly paired opponent and episode while rejecting cross-linked events.

accepted.s: The conflict with which opponent began during the reign of Prola II?
accepted.x: The Kakatiya conflict with the Yadavas, also called the Sevunas of Devagiri, began during the reign of Prola II.
accepted.tq: Link the beginning of the conflict to the correct opponent and period.

accepted.s: Who killed Prola II?
accepted.x: The Velanati Chodas killed Prola II. Rudradeva later avenged him and appointed Vellanki Gangadhara as viceroy of Sabbinadu.
accepted.tq: Apply the strongest history trap: match the ruler with the correct opponent responsible for his death.

accepted.s: In 1159, Rudradeva defeated which group of opponents?
accepted.x: In 1159, Rudradeva defeated the Kalachuri confederacy leaders Mailagi, Medaraja of Polavasa and Dommaraja of Nagumuru.
accepted.tq: Anchor the year to the specific group of opponents rather than to the better-known later wars.

accepted.s: Which of the following was defeated by Rudradeva?
accepted.x: Rudradeva defeated the Telugu Chodas and Tailapa III. The Muttukur victory over Ganapatideva belonged to the Pandyas, while Ballala III was defeated later by Pedarudru.
accepted.tq: Find the option assigning a later or different ruler’s victory to Rudradeva.

accepted.s: Which statement regarding the succession after Ganapatideva is correct?
o: Ganapatideva had no son, and Rudrama Devi succeeded him after being raised as a son or putrika.
Ganapatideva’s son succeeded him, while Rudrama Devi remained outside the succession.
Ganapatideva was succeeded by his sister Mailamba after appointing Rudrama Devi as a feudatory.
Rudrama Devi succeeded only after the Kakatiya kingdom was annexed by the Yadavas.
accepted.x: Ganapatideva had no son. Rudrama Devi was raised as a son, or putrika, and succeeded him.
accepted.tq: Use the succession exception—daughter raised as a son—to reject the conventional son-successor trap.

accepted.s: Rudrama Devi ruled during which period?
accepted.x: Rudrama Devi succeeded Ganapatideva and ruled from 1262 to 1289.
accepted.tq: Compare the closely spaced reign periods and select the one belonging to Rudrama Devi.

accepted.s: Who guided Rudrama Devi’s training?
accepted.x: Kupama Devi, Rudrama Devi’s mother, guided her training when she was being raised as a son.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the mother who guided training from the sisters and daughter mentioned in the succession account.

accepted.s: Ganapatideva’s sisters Mailamba and Kundamamba were married to whom?
o: The princes of the Yadava house
accepted.x: Mailamba and Kundamamba married the sons of Natavadi Buddharaja, namely Rudra and his brother.
accepted.tq: Use the family-relationship clue to distinguish the sisters’ marriages from Ganapatideva’s daughters’ marriages.

accepted.s: Which statement best describes the political significance of the Kakatiyas?
o: They were the second dynasty after the Satavahanas to unify all Telugu-speaking regions and the first to rule all Telugu-speakers.
They were the first dynasty after the Satavahanas to rule only the coastal Telugu region.
They were the second dynasty after the Satavahanas to establish a purely Sanskrit-speaking administration.
They ruled the Andhra region only after the foundation of Vijayanagara.
accepted.x: The Kakatiyas are described as the second dynasty after the Satavahanas to unite the Andhra region and the first to rule all Telugu-speaking regions.
accepted.tq: Separate the scope of territorial unification from language and chronological distractors.

accepted.s: From which ruler’s reign did Telugu replace Sanskrit in Kakatiya inscriptions?
accepted.x: Telugu replaced Sanskrit in inscriptions from the reign of Ganapatideva. More than 1,000 Kakatiya inscriptions are known.
accepted.tq: Match the language change with the correct reign rather than with the beginning or end of the dynasty.

accepted.s: The Archaeological Survey of India’s June 2026 Nallamala survey copied Kakatiya inscriptions among how many records dating from the second to the sixteenth century?
accepted.x: The survey copied Kakatiya inscriptions among 25 records dating from the second to the sixteenth century.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact current-affairs figure and reject nearby numerical distractors.

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Ramappa Temple at Palampet?
o: It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site inscribed in 2016 and is noted for a circular platform and granite bricks.
It was built at Nellore and is noted for its rectangular platform and wooden roof.
It was constructed by the Pandyas at Muttukur and is noted for its floating stones.
It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site inscribed in 2021 and is noted for its star-shaped platform and floating bricks.
accepted.x: The Ramappa Temple at Palampet became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2021 and is noted for its star-shaped platform and floating bricks.
accepted.tq: Combine the location, recognition year and distinctive architectural features before selecting the complete description.

accepted.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order:
A. First mention of the Kakatiyas at Magallu
B. Accession of Rudradeva as the first sovereign Kakatiya
C. Defeat of Ganapatideva at Muttukur
D. Rule of Rudrama Devi
accepted.x: The first mention at Magallu was in 956, Rudradeva became the first sovereign in 1163, Ganapatideva was defeated at Muttukur in 1263, and Rudrama Devi ruled from 1262 to 1289; in the stated sequence, the intended chronological order is A, B, C, D.
accepted.tq: Start with the earliest dated reference and place the reign and battle dates in ascending order.

accepted.s: Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?
o: Magallu — First mention of the Kakatiyas, 956
Ganapatideva — First mention of the Kakatiyas, 956
accepted.x: The first mention of the Kakatiyas is associated with Magallu in 956. Rudradeva was the first sovereign in 1163, while Prataparudra II was the last ruler.
accepted.tq: Use the first–last distinction and attach each date to the correct historical milestone.

accepted.s: Who is regarded as the last ruler of the Kakatiya dynasty?
accepted.x: Prataparudra II is identified as the last ruler of the Kakatiya dynasty.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the last ruler from the major earlier sovereigns and the female successor.
